name: Subclavian vein
notes: Drains into the brachiocephalic vein; continuation of the axillary vein.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Axillary vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Cephalic vein
notes: Superficial vein, ascends the lateral arm/forearm, drains into the axillary v. via the deltopectoral groove/clavipectoral fascia (piercing point).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Basilic vein
notes: Superficial vein, ascends the medial forearm/arm, pierces deep fascia at the mid-arm to join the brachial veins forming the axillary v.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Median cubital vein
notes: Connects cephalic and basilic veins across the cubital fossa; classic venipuncture site.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Brachial veins (venae comitantes)
notes: Paired deep veins accompanying the brachial artery.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Radial veins (venae comitantes)
supplies_or_drains: deep lateral forearm, accompanying radial artery territory
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Ulnar veins (venae comitantes)
supplies_or_drains: deep medial forearm, accompanying ulnar artery territory
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Dorsal venous network of the hand
notes: Superficial plexus draining the hand; origin of the cephalic (radial side) and basilic (ulnar side) veins.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Median antebrachial vein
supplies_or_drains: superficial palmar aspect and volar forearm
notes: Ascends the middle of the volar forearm and drains variably into the basilic vein, the median cubital, or both after dividing into median basilic and median cephalic veins.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Accessory cephalic vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Perforating veins of the forearm
supplies_or_drains: connections from the superficial to the deep venous system
notes: Valved to direct flow from superficial to deep, the same arrangement as in the leg, although upper limb valvular incompetence is rarely clinically significant.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Thoracoepigastric vein
supplies_or_drains: lateral trunk wall, linking the axillary and femoral venous systems
notes: A caval collateral channel: it distends visibly on the lateral chest and abdominal wall in inferior vena cava obstruction.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Dorsal metacarpal veins
supplies_or_drains: dorsum of the hand and the interdigital spaces
notes: Feed the dorsal venous network, the origin of both the cephalic and basilic veins and the standard site for peripheral cannulation.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
